design-status.name: README/design-status-01
design-status.text: The current command journeys and their observed evidence are described in the conformance record. The seven comparison requirements remain published as uncovered: command execution alone does not establish model correspondence. The aligned models and their retained reference definitions build with the pinned Lean compiler; their proofs establish their stated model propositions.

design-status.name: README/design-status-02
design-status.text: The old executable corpora and playable simulator have been retired. The documentation archive carries the retained model source and its checksums. The economics paper keeps its historical model revision and proof references; those references do not describe the current library's theorem inventory.

design-status.name: README/design-status-03
design-status.text: Build and serve the documentation with the pinned Nix toolchain.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-01
how-the-parts-fit.text: The diagram and table below record the original three-operation design. The current commands support registration and permanent termination; the five other historical edge encodings are refused. Application payload updates remain local to the application output. The original design is retained here as historical context.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-02
how-the-parts-fit.text: The application keeps its state in the UTxO holding the NFT and controls its own local transitions; the registry never sees that state. Singular records only whether a key has an outstanding representative or has been permanently retired, and enforces the coupling between registry transitions and NFT supply.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-03
how-the-parts-fit.text: Active and Over contain no application payload. Registry Update means retirement, not an application-state update. Over is terminal.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-04
how-the-parts-fit.text: The configured application policy ID is the authorization anchor. It mints action tokens whose asset names hash the action and its necessary parameters. Insert approval binds the registry/key, initial application datum and destination. Withdraw approval separately binds the exact pending Insert and its refund requirements; Insert approval alone cannot authorize cancellation.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-05
how-the-parts-fit.text: Insert carries no representative NFT, can fail at folding if its key is occupied, and can be withdrawn with the required authorization. Update/Delete carry the existing representative after the application authorizes its exact release, and retain it until completion. The concrete request-token arrangement for Update/Delete remains open.

how-the-parts-fit.name: README/how-the-parts-fit-06
how-the-parts-fit.text: Read the original responsibilities, request lifecycle and certification rules as historical design context. To run the current commands, start with Demo 1, then read the registry command guide and consumer conformance record.

install.name: README/install-01
install.text: From the release after 0.13.1, without Nix. On a Mac with Apple Silicon:

install.name: README/install-02
install.text: On Linux on x86_64, download singular-X.Y.Z-x86_64-linux.deb or singular-X.Y.Z-x86_64-linux.rpm from the releases page and install it with your package manager, or run the AppImage of a command. Each of them gives singular, open-datum and devnet, the private development node Demo 1 starts, and, except the AppImages, the deployment blueprint the commands take as --blueprint. The install page has the commands, the checksums and the tarballs that hold all three in one folder.

singular.name: README/singular-00
singular.text: Not for mainnet. Do not deploy Singular or open datum on mainnet until on-chain verification and an independent audit are complete.

singular.name: README/singular-02
singular.text: A permissionless registry on Cardano for unique identities and independent application state.

start-here-play-demo-1.name: README/start-here-play-demo-1-01
start-here-play-demo-1.text: As a Cardano developer who knows cardano-cli, wallets, faucets and Koios but not Singular, you can play Demo 1, a registry from creation to termination in sixteen steps, and watch every step either succeed or be refused where the page says it will. The Demo 1 page says what the play shows and where to play it: the step-by-step page of singular-demo, with a copy button on every block; its Nix shell, which holds singular, open-datum and a private development chain; and its Ubuntu kit for a machine without Nix. To play it in a browser with nothing installed, open the Killercoda scenario; to watch it without running anything, open the recorded run.

who-this-is-for.name: README/who-this-is-for-01
who-this-is-for.text: An application developer wants keys that are unique across everyone using the application — names, identifiers, handles — without running a registrar. They supply one parameter, their application policy ID, and get a registry in which every active key is represented by exactly one NFT sitting in one of their own application outputs. Singular mints that NFT when a certified registration is folded in, burns it when the key is retired or released, and lets a released key be registered again.

who-this-is-for.name: README/who-this-is-for-02
who-this-is-for.text: A user of that application asks it to register a key. The application approves the exact proposal — including the refund address stored in the request — and the request waits, holding no NFT, until someone folds it into the registry. Before folding, a separately authorized cancellation copies that stored refund address and leaves the name free; redirecting the refund, relying only on Insert certification, cancelling after fold, or replaying cancellation is refused. The registry fixes where a deposit returns, never its amount: no fee, price or bond rule is part of it.

who-this-is-for.name: README/who-this-is-for-03
who-this-is-for.text: A folder — anyone at all — collects pending requests and applies them to the registry in one transaction. There is no owner to sign, no privileged actor, and no way to fold a request that does not satisfy the protocol.

who-this-is-for.name: README/who-this-is-for-04
who-this-is-for.text: A resolver wants to know whether a key is active and where its application state currently lives. It authenticates the registry entry, finds the NFT, and reads the application's own output. A key that is retired or in a pending terminal request yields no live state.

who-this-is-for.name: README/who-this-is-for-05
who-this-is-for.text: A Cardano developer who wants to try it plays the whole thing on a private test chain from a page of steps to copy, signing with a vault wallet whose key stays sealed in a file on their machine, or signing on another machine. The Demo 1 page says what the play shows and links the steps.

build-and-check.name: docs-building/build-and-check-02
build-and-check.text: The documentation package and checks use the locked shared MkDocs toolchain. The documentation check inspects rendered internal links, section anchors, navigation, speech data and theme assets. The aligned models build through just application-held-model and just open-datum-application-held-model; their proofs do not establish application behavior.

building-the-documentation.name: docs-building/building-the-documentation-01
building-the-documentation.text: The site renders the repository's canonical Markdown and specification. A generated staging directory preserves their relative paths; it is not a second editable documentation tree.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-01
documentation-releases.text: The documentation version is the one version.txt, the release manifest and the changelog agree on; a prepared version is not evidence that an archive was tagged or published. Release-please's simple strategy updates those three surfaces together for later versions, and Nix requires the version and manifest to agree. These are documentation versions, not deployed protocol versions.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-02
documentation-releases.text: After a successful main-branch gate, repository-scoped App credentials let release-please prepare a release PR whose changes trigger normal CI. It plans PRs only: release creation is disabled because upstream release creation posts a PR comment. Merging the release PR prepares the version but does not tag or publish it. An operator-authorized v<version> tag on that merged release PR's exact commit triggers publication. The commit must belong to main, and tag, manifest and version must agree.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-03
documentation-releases.text: The tag workflow builds and checks a Nix-produced documentation archive and checksum, publishes them to the matching GitHub release, downloads and verifies the uploaded bytes, then changes the release PR's pending label to tagged. It accepts a pending or already-tagged matching PR so interrupted publication can be retried. It does not post PR comments. CI has a manual recovery trigger; no release workflow or tag is dispatched merely by adding this automation.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-04
documentation-releases.text: Build the documentation archive locally with nix build .#docs-release, and run version, workflow and artifact checks with nix run .#release-check. The archive contains the rendered site, speech data and retained model sources under artifacts/lean/. Its inner artifacts/SHA256SUMS binds those source bytes; the outer SHA256SUMS binds the archive. It contains no retired corpus or simulator replay workspace.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-05
documentation-releases.text: After extraction, run sha256sum --check artifacts/SHA256SUMS to verify the source files. This checksum check establishes byte integrity, not model execution or implementation correspondence. Published releases are listed at https://github.com/lambdasistemi/singular/releases.

documentation-releases.name: docs-building/documentation-releases-06
documentation-releases.text: The initial empty-manifest behavior and version override follow the release-please manifest documentation. Publishing remains a separate action from reviewing this documentation.

edit-and-serve.name: docs-building/edit-and-serve-01
edit-and-serve.text: The development shell has a separate CI build because packaged builds do not exercise it:

edit-and-serve.name: docs-building/edit-and-serve-02
edit-and-serve.text: just build-docs and just serve-docs stage the generated API references from the packaged site build, nix build .#docs, so the local site links the same generated pages the packaged site and its checks carry; the Markdown pages still reload live as they are edited.

edit-and-serve.name: docs-building/edit-and-serve-03
edit-and-serve.text: To serve the packaged output without a live-reload editor, run the docs-serve tool (marked not-a-guarantee) with the port as its argument and open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

generated-api-references.name: docs-building/generated-api-references-01
generated-api-references.text: The site ships a generated reference for each library a contributor calls into, built from the same revision as the pages that link it. Which code has one, and what stands in for it where there is none:

generated-api-references.name: docs-building/generated-api-references-02
generated-api-references.text: Executables, test suites and the runtime service modules outside the library's extent have no generated pages here. That coverage gap stays visible, exactly as the off-chain reference's own page records it: wider generated coverage is a separate decision for the epic's owner, not one this page takes. Each generated reference carries a manifest binding its pages to the digests of the source it was generated from, and the documentation check fails when a page, its source or its link targets no longer agree.

haskell-formatting.name: docs-building/haskell-formatting-01
haskell-formatting.text: The repository's Haskell trees are formatted with Fourmolu under one house configuration, fourmolu.yaml at the repository root. Every formatter entrypoint — the off-chain lint check, the Conformance format check and the root recipes below — passes that file explicitly, so a missing configuration fails loudly instead of falling back to Fourmolu's defaults, and there is no per-tree configuration to drift from it.

haskell-formatting.name: docs-building/haskell-formatting-02
haskell-formatting.text: Discovery is dynamic: every Haskell source under offchain/ and conformance/ — the formerly fenced verifier sources and the evaluation spike included — with no directory exclusions, so a new file or component directory is covered with nothing to edit. The Conformance tree gets the same check in its own Nix source context through nix run .#format-check from conformance/ (CI job 'Conformance Haskell format and lint check'). just format-controls runs the negative and positive controls: a source that Fourmolu's defaults accept but the house configuration rejects must fail the check — proving the configuration is read — and its formatter correction must pass it again; a tree without the configuration must fail loudly rather than format with defaults; a newly tracked component tree outside the old directories joins the check through the Git index, while ignored untracked build noise never enters it and a tracked file under an ignored path stays. The controls run over scratch copies and never touch the working tree.

haskell-formatting.name: docs-building/haskell-formatting-03
haskell-formatting.text: HLint runs over the same discovered extent with no exclusions and no ignore file: nix run .#lint from offchain/ (CI job 'Off-chain lint') checks both formats and hints, and nix run .#hlint-check from conformance/ runs beside the Conformance format check.

ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.name: docs-building/ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-builds-00
ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.text: Ordinary binaries and explicit test builds.

ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.name: docs-building/ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-builds-01
ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.text: As a release operator, I build ordinary singular and open-datum with the manual Cabal test-harness flag disabled. Both executable closures use the ordinary registry CLI modules. The release archive and publication commands select these ordinary outputs.

ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.name: docs-building/ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-builds-02
ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.text: As a contributor, I exercise crash windows and provider-answer loss with the separately named test outputs. Their registry CLI modules retain the original hold/drop controls and SINGULAR_HARNESS_TRIE_TRACE, an independent observation of the trie capability's actual operations. That diagnostic is a hidden test input and its evidence belongs to the test build.

ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.name: docs-building/ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-builds-03
ordinary-binaries-and-explicit-test-buil.text: The build control strips and inspects both ordinary compiled executables, reads the actual resolved registry CLI flag, and deliberately rejects the hook-bearing test artifacts and opposite flag polarity. CLI recovery and conformance backend controls select the explicit test composition. Test outputs are never substituted into the ordinary release verifier or published as ordinary release artifacts.

other-languages.name: docs-building/other-languages-01
other-languages.text: Every other code family the inventory discovers is linted and format-checked by one command, over the inventory's own extent, with the tools the development shell pins:

other-languages.name: docs-building/other-languages-02
other-languages.text: Lean and HTML have no general formatter here, so the explicit style rules are the policy: no tab, no carriage return, no trailing whitespace, and exactly one final newline. Aiken sources are checked by aiken fmt --check inside the onchain/ and application on-chain flake checks, with the Aiken each flake pins; formatting leaves every compiled validator and its hash unchanged. Generated preimage vectors are regenerated from their formatted sources, and their freshness check stays the policy. A code family nobody checks fails just lint instead of passing silently.

publication-and-accessibility.name: docs-building/publication-and-accessibility-01
publication-and-accessibility.text: Pull requests publish to a live preview with the candidate revision recorded alongside the generated site. Preview publication does not post PR comments. The default branch publishes through workflow-mode GitHub Pages after merge; the same documentation build supplies both routes.

publication-and-accessibility.name: docs-building/publication-and-accessibility-02
publication-and-accessibility.text: The Terminal theme follows the system light/dark preference until a reader chooses with the toggle, and remembers that choice. Diagrams follow the same palette and open at full size in a viewer. Each section has a play button that speaks the recorded narration of its paragraphs in the Puck voice. The voice says the page text word for word: the speech companions are written by the extraction tool, which reads the prose of each rendered page, and tables, code blocks and diagrams are not spoken. The documentation check fails when a paragraph changed without its recording. just extract-speech rewrites the companions after a page edit and just narrate records the paragraphs that changed; recording needs a DeepInfra key. Diagrams are Mermaid, rendered by the copy the shared toolchain pins as a fixed-output Nix input and served from the site itself; no page loads a script or stylesheet from outside the site, and the site check fails if one does.

the-repository-code-inventory.name: docs-building/the-repository-code-inventory-01
the-repository-code-inventory.text: just inventory maps every file the tree actually holds to its lint policy and its format policy — or, for data and artifacts, to a named non-code class — and fails on anything unmapped. Discovery walks the tree itself (extensions, shebangs, executable mode and component manifests), so a new source file in a covered directory is mapped without editing anything, while a file nobody classified fails with a named diagnostic instead of passing silently. The same inventory runs over the Nix flake source, where no Git directory exists, through nix run .#inventory-check; pull-request CI runs both forms so the two contexts cannot drift. The checked registry lives in tools/code_inventory.py.

the-repository-code-inventory.name: docs-building/the-repository-code-inventory-02
the-repository-code-inventory.text: The inventory is a mapping, not enforcement: its report names the CI carrier that executes each policy, and every lint and format policy is enforced — no code family is left without a checker, and no source directory is excluded. just inventory-controls runs the negative and positive controls: synthetic orphans injected into scratch copies of the classified tree, each required to produce its intended failure. The controls never touch the working tree.

recovering-a-registry-command.name: docs-cli-recovery/recovering-a-registry-command-01
recovering-a-registry-command.text: As an operator creating a registry, booking a registration, updating a holding or terminating its key, you need an interrupted transaction to keep its identity so the next write can reconcile it without sending it twice. The retained commands are described in the registry command guide.

recovering-a-registry-command.name: docs-cli-recovery/recovering-a-registry-command-02
recovering-a-registry-command.text: The former reader has replacement: none, issue 744. Recovery is performed by the next write using its journal and the public chain.

the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.name: docs-cli-recovery/the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-register-keys-00
the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.text: The commands that create a registry and register keys.

the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.name: docs-cli-recovery/the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-register-keys-01
the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.text: As Carol, Alice or Bob running one of the commands of create a registry and register keys on the proved design, you are interrupted in the same ways as above and promised the same thing: the transaction keeps its identity, the next write settles it, and nothing is sent a second time.

the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.name: docs-cli-recovery/the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-register-keys-02
the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.text: Each transaction is journalled as prepared before it is sent, under the step that names it: publish-state-script, publish-application-script and create for open datum's first creation, publish-scripts and create for Singular's, then book, fold, reclaim and cleanup. The journal also records what the first output of the transaction must hold once it is on the chain: a reference script for a publication, the state token for a creation and for a fold, the approval token for a booking, a payment to the refund address for a reclaim and a cleanup. A creation is journalled under the application and the wallet, because the name of the registry it makes is known only once its seed is chosen. The other commands are journalled under the registry and the wallet.

the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.name: docs-cli-recovery/the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-register-keys-03
the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.text: Before it builds anything, the next write of the same wallet reads its journal against the chain. The table shows what it does with an earlier transaction in each case.

the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.name: docs-cli-recovery/the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-register-keys-04
the-commands-that-create-a-registry-and-.text: A transaction the chain does not show cannot be told from one the network has not yet delivered, and these commands never declare it excluded: the next write keeps naming it and stops. Wait for the network and run the command again; a transaction that lands is reconciled. When it can never land, the way out is --state-dir naming another state directory, which starts a fresh journal for that registry and wallet, or for a creation, for that application and wallet; the old journal stays as a record.

what-the-checks-show.name: docs-cli-recovery/what-the-checks-show-01
what-the-checks-show.text: The recovery controls run the commands of the proved design as separate singular and open-datum processes against one generated development node per partition. Each sending command is interrupted three ways: the node takes its transaction but the answer is lost, the process is killed after sending, and the command prepares a transaction without sending it. The checks read the process receipts, managed journals and saved signed bodies. The node's own devnet probe confirms the outputs used to reach each holding.

what-the-checks-show.name: docs-cli-recovery/what-the-checks-show-02
what-the-checks-show.text: The root flake declares the four retained partitions. Discovery prints their complete list for the workflow matrix; the census refuses empty discovery, unknown parts, duplicate parts and missing parts. Each partition runs by key:

what-the-checks-show.name: docs-cli-recovery/what-the-checks-show-03
what-the-checks-show.text: Each interrupted transaction keeps exactly one prepared identity and a saved body whose hash matches its journal entry. A later write by the same wallet observes an included transaction exactly once. While an unsent transaction remains unresolved, the next write stops with that identity and case; its journal does not move and it builds or sends nothing. No command automatically resubmits the interrupted transaction.

what-the-checks-show.name: docs-cli-recovery/what-the-checks-show-04
what-the-checks-show.text: Every partition retains its original receipts, journals and signed bodies under their source-relative paths, with a manifest binding the candidate, run, partition and file hashes. The workflow verifies those hashes and records from both wallets before uploading each partition separately. The receipt guard refuses more than 52428800 bytes and accepts that boundary.

what-the-checks-show.name: docs-cli-recovery/what-the-checks-show-05
what-the-checks-show.text: The current line's history, rollback, two-request and cross-wallet recovery scenarios have been retired with their old bootstrap. Their trie observations are not evidence for the retained commands. The separate facade lifecycle controls continue to exercise fatal failure, restart, cancellation and joined cleanup on their generated node. These checks establish process interruption and recovery over the exercised cases, not durability across a power loss.

conformance-api-reference.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/conformance-api-reference-01
conformance-api-reference.text: As a contributor changing the evidence reader, I can open each module's interface and highlighted source at the same revision as this site. The generated Haddock reference covers the receipt validation, replay classification, requirement inventory and computed evidence page.

how-the-reference-stays-honest.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/how-the-reference-stays-honest-01
how-the-reference-stays-honest.text: The reference cannot drift from the code it claims to document. The site build derives a manifest from the same Conformance source input Haddock ran on: for every module it records the digest of the Haskell source file and the digests of the actual generated module page and source page. The site check then redoes both halves independently from this repository's own source tree — the manifest's module extent must equal the Cabal library extent, each recorded source digest must match the repository's file, and each generated page in the shipped site must match its recorded digest. A reference generated from any other source, however its label reads, fails that comparison; a page edited after generation fails its own digest.

how-the-reference-stays-honest.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/how-the-reference-stays-honest-02
how-the-reference-stays-honest.text: Every link inside the generated pages is inspected too. A reference from one module of this library to another — a type, a function, a module, however the tool that generated it spelled it — must resolve to a page of this reference and, where it names an anchor, to an anchor that exists. The check prints how many same-library links it resolved, and this page's links to the generated pages are checked by the site's ordinary link inventory.

how-the-reference-stays-honest.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/how-the-reference-stays-honest-03
how-the-reference-stays-honest.text: Dependency documentation is a different matter. The library is built against a JSON, container and text dependency closure, and none of those packages' Haddock pages are bundled into this site: a type such as an aeson value or a strict text appears in the generated pages as a visible label, but it is not a link — following it would leave this site for documentation that is not shipped with it. Neutralizing those labels is decided from the build's own package database, which positively names every module each dependency owns, so a label is only unlinked when it provably belongs to a dependency; a dead or store-path link that reappears fails the site check, and a same-library reference may never be treated as a dependency label to hide a broken link.

how-the-reference-stays-honest.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/how-the-reference-stays-honest-04
how-the-reference-stays-honest.text: One further generator class is unlinked by structure. Haddock renders instance method names in each instance's Methods list as same-page links, but emits no matching anchors for them — every instance of a class lists the same method names, so the anchor would have to be duplicated. Those method labels stay visible as plain text inside the instance lists, and the site check both counts them separately and still requires every fragment link outside that exact structure to resolve.

how-the-reference-stays-honest.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/how-the-reference-stays-honest-05
how-the-reference-stays-honest.text: The release archive check extends the same discipline to what gets shipped: the staged documentation archive must carry this library's generated reference member for member and byte for byte, alongside the off-chain registry library's, before the ordinary release checks run.

what-the-reference-does-not-claim.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/what-the-reference-does-not-claim-00
what-the-reference-does-not-claim.text: What the reference does not claim.

what-the-reference-does-not-claim.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/what-the-reference-does-not-claim-01
what-the-reference-does-not-claim.text: API documentation does not establish product conformance. The seven application-held comparison requirements remain uncovered in the consumer record and the generated evidence page. The appendix tests check the reader; development-network journeys are a separate evidence boundary and do not establish model agreement.

what-this-reference-contains.name: docs-conformance-api-reference/what-this-reference-contains-01
what-this-reference-contains.text: Every module declared by the public Conformance library is listed below. The site derives the extent from its Cabal manifest and checks both each module page and its source page against that extent. The reference's own full-page index and symbol index provide the same entry points across the complete library.

design-choices.name: docs-conformance-architecture/design-choices-01
design-choices.text: Read the consumer record for commands and the generated evidence page for the complete requirements and their computed standings.

inputs-and-responsibilities.name: docs-conformance-architecture/inputs-and-responsibilities-01
inputs-and-responsibilities.text: The receipt loader checks report identities, outcomes, measurements, refusal attribution, replay provenance, duplicate requirements and the size bound. The overlay matches a report to its requirement and code revision. Without such a report the reader publishes the coverage plan. The page refuses a snapshot whose reports or contract results name another revision or a dirty tree, and refuses inconsistent contract-case lists across adapters.

ownership-and-limits.name: docs-conformance-architecture/ownership-and-limits-01
ownership-and-limits.text: The caller supplies the receipt directory. Each command reads its inventory and inputs for its own invocation; the reader starts no node or background worker. Tests own their temporary report directories for one example and remove them when the example finishes.

ownership-and-limits.name: docs-conformance-architecture/ownership-and-limits-02
ownership-and-limits.text: The seven application-held comparisons remain uncovered. Their development- network journeys are separate observations and supply no model-comparison credit. The backend-contract snapshot retains its own revision and source provenance in the appendix. Neither reader tests nor a green coverage ratchet establish the missing comparisons.

reading-conformance-evidence.name: docs-conformance-architecture/reading-conformance-evidence-01
reading-conformance-evidence.text: As an integrator, I want every published comparison requirement to stay visible when its evidence is missing, and every reported result to name the revision it checked. The reader separates the inventory's coverage plan from the receipts that can change a requirement's standing.

check-the-reader.name: docs-consumer-conformance/check-the-reader-01
check-the-reader.text: The appendix tests check the evidence reader. The coverage ratchet reports regressions against its protected base. Neither command supplies the missing model comparisons. The aligned models remain at the application-held model and the open-datum model.

consumer-conformance-record.name: docs-consumer-conformance/consumer-conformance-record-01
consumer-conformance-record.text: As an integrator, I can read the registration, holding update, termination, reading, shared-publication and batch-fold requirements and see which comparisons have evidence. The generated evidence page publishes every requirement, including the ones no run has demonstrated.

consumer-conformance-record.name: docs-consumer-conformance/consumer-conformance-record-02
consumer-conformance-record.text: This summary is computed from the same inventory and validated receipts as the evidence page, for code revision c17309ee607368615b96f23ea4f96401467195f5. Separate command journeys and measurements do not grant model-comparison credit.

consumer-conformance-record.name: docs-consumer-conformance/consumer-conformance-record-03
consumer-conformance-record.text: The registration and holding requirements compare the previous and application-held designs. Their old side is computed from the retained Lean model. The development-network journey and refusal jobs are separate observations; they establish the transactions they run and do not establish agreement with the model.

creating-on-shared-publications.name: docs-consumer-conformance/creating-on-shared-publications-01
creating-on-shared-publications.text: The shared-publication requirements describe a later creation reusing both scripts, an independent creator reusing them from the chain, separation between application releases, registration in a registry created on shared copies and measured creation costs. Their standings are computed from matching receipts, alongside the preceding requirements. Publication measurements supply no model-comparison credit. The comparison and reading requirements keep their previous contents and receipt-derived standings.

creating-on-shared-publications.name: docs-consumer-conformance/creating-on-shared-publications-02
creating-on-shared-publications.text: The registration journey, recovery partitions and checked measurement receipts are separate evidence boundaries. They show the packaged commands and measured transactions they run and nothing about agreement with the model. An executable conformance language for creation claims is outside this change. The reuse guide shows the commands and discovery receipt fields; the cost comparison reads its figures from receipts.

folding-a-batch-from-public-data.name: docs-consumer-conformance/folding-a-batch-from-public-data-00
folding-a-batch-from-public-data.text: Folding a batch from public data.

folding-a-batch-from-public-data.name: docs-consumer-conformance/folding-a-batch-from-public-data-01
folding-a-batch-from-public-data.text: As a folder, I find and fold registrations and terminations of a registry without any file from their booker. The batch requirements describe public discovery, named skips, the folder's surplus, the largest fitting prefix and what remains, explicit batches and state-policy refusals, and measured limits. The summary computes their standings from model-comparison receipts. Selection order and capacity are operational facts; the model states no network-size rule.

folding-a-batch-from-public-data.name: docs-consumer-conformance/folding-a-batch-from-public-data-02
folding-a-batch-from-public-data.text: The packaged registration journey, batch refusals and batch measurement are separate evidence boundaries. They show the commands and transactions they execute, and evaluation of kept transactions under recorded parameters, with development-node corroboration. They establish nothing about agreement with the model. The folder guide describes the commands, receipt and limits; its figures are generated from the committed measurement.

read-the-evidence.name: docs-consumer-conformance/read-the-evidence-01
read-the-evidence.text: The inventory carries a coverage plan. Only validated receipts for the stated revision can establish execution. The generated page leaves requirements without those receipts visible as uncovered. Its marked appendix preserves the generic backend-contract snapshot with its original code revision and source provenance; those results do not cover the comparison requirements.

reading-from-a-registry-address.name: docs-consumer-conformance/reading-from-a-registry-address-01
reading-from-a-registry-address.text: As a reader, I give a registry address and key without a signer, blueprint or local registry state. The reading requirements describe the neutral key status, open datum's live holding and pending termination, measured provider calls, rows and bytes with another registry's holdings at the same address, and named refusals. Their standings are computed in the summary above. The command observations below supply no executable comparison with the application-held model.

reading-from-a-registry-address.name: docs-consumer-conformance/reading-from-a-registry-address-02
reading-from-a-registry-address.text: The registration journey runs both packaged readers at connected live, pending and terminal checkpoints and reads an unused key. Its artifact includes the answers and a known-key query measurement. The registration refusals job runs wrong-network, unknown-policy and failed-provider reads beside passing controls. These are separate command observations, with controls that reject altered answers; they establish nothing about agreement with the model. See reading a key for the commands and settings, and the generated evidence page for receipt-derived standings.

can-creation-carry-its-scripts.name: docs-creation-cost/can-creation-carry-its-scripts-01
can-creation-carry-its-scripts.text: The measuring tool built 5 registry-creation forms with the real genesis and application configuration builders, on one fresh development network with the same frozen protocol parameters as the comparison above. Each form creates a fresh registry with the same configuration; only script placement changes. The normal referenced form is the reference point. These are experiments, and the production command keeps its shared publications.

can-creation-carry-its-scripts.name: docs-creation-cost/can-creation-carry-its-scripts-02
can-creation-carry-its-scripts.text: Both live copies were available for this controlled experiment. A form carrying a script deliberately ignores that script's live copy. A form creating reference outputs also carries witnesses: a transaction cannot read its own new outputs as reference inputs.

can-creation-carry-its-scripts.name: docs-creation-cost/can-creation-carry-its-scripts-03
can-creation-carry-its-scripts.text: The state-carried form has 8764 complete signed bytes and the application-carried form has 10821. The node accepted and confirmed both mixed forms. Each still needs the other script's live reference output.

can-creation-carry-its-scripts.name: docs-creation-cost/can-creation-carry-its-scripts-04
can-creation-carry-its-scripts.text: Carrying both scripts in witnesses has 18567 complete signed bytes; carrying them in witnesses and new reference outputs has 36292. The node refused both for maximum transaction size: it counts 18566 and 36291 bytes respectively, against a limit of 16384. The complete signed transaction length and the length the ledger counts are different figures; the ledger count here is one byte less. Both appear below.

can-creation-carry-its-scripts.name: docs-creation-cost/can-creation-carry-its-scripts-05
can-creation-carry-its-scripts.text: A fit requires successful execution, size within the ledger limit, and the development node's acceptance and confirmation. The execution figures are the ledger evaluator's final results on the actual chain inputs and equal the signed execution budgets. The oversized forms were evaluated locally, then refused by the node's size check before its script-execution phase; their execution figures do not claim node execution. A size comparison alone is never reported as a fit.

candidate-design.name: docs-creation-cost/candidate-design-01
candidate-design.text: Release: open-datum 0.17.0 (commit ede9f7992c4936474d3ed86f890ffa2e6fddf625). Revision: ede9f7992c4936474d3ed86f890ffa2e6fddf625. Deployment blueprint SHA-256: 6ad16a3194cff51f0600edfe0eb95917ed0679693e1e4b6f332ad1072c07d3d1.

finding-a-shared-script.name: docs-creation-cost/finding-a-shared-script-01
finding-a-shared-script.text: As a creator, you can reuse another wallet's live publications with your own wallet and a fresh state directory. You need the release and your provider settings, but no file or address from the publisher. The provider finds candidate live outputs by script hash. The command computes the hash of each carried script, including its language and applied parameters, before deciding whether to reuse it.

finding-a-shared-script.name: docs-creation-cost/finding-a-shared-script-02
finding-a-shared-script.text: Each script in the creation receipt has one outcome: reused or published. Its discovery record retains the candidate references, the hashes found and expected, and whether each candidate is genuine or foreign. A foreign candidate is skipped even if another genuine copy is reused. No live copy means none was found by this provider; the unspent-output query cannot distinguish a spent output from one that never existed.

finding-a-shared-script.name: docs-creation-cost/finding-a-shared-script-03
finding-a-shared-script.text: This is discovery by script hash through the configured provider. Publishing references for everyone, naming a trusted publisher and general public discovery remain outside this workflow, in issues 355 and 473. No witness-policy publication or witness-pin configuration is needed.

finding-a-shared-script.name: docs-creation-cost/finding-a-shared-script-04
finding-a-shared-script.text: After an interruption around publication, rerunning reuses what is live and publishes only what is missing. An uncertain submission keeps its saved transaction identity and signed body; a later invocation reconciles it without automatically resubmitting it. Create is not idempotent: a further invocation can create another registry from a new seed. Repeating an explicit seed that has already been spent retains the existing refusal.

frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters.name: docs-creation-cost/frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters-01
frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters.text: Every form used maximum transaction size 16384, maximum transaction execution memory 140000000 and maximum transaction execution steps 10000000000. The parameters and their hash are read from the independent chain record, rather than supplied by the measuring command.

frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters.name: docs-creation-cost/frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters-02
frozen-limits-and-fee-parameters.text: The experiment holds the application's configuration fixed across forms. These explicit experimental values do not change command defaults.

limits.name: docs-creation-cost/limits-01
limits.text: These are development-network measurements, not fee quotes for another network. Reference-output capital is reported separately from fees; this page does not claim it is spent. The measured transactions do not establish public reference discovery for everyone, batch limits or release acceptance. Those remain the work of issues 355 and 473, issue 746 and issue 747 respectively. Existing uncovered registration comparisons remain uncovered.

limits.name: docs-creation-cost/limits-02
limits.text: Creation behavior remains bound to the application-held model's genesis and recognition inversions, creation money statement, configuration creation inversion and immutable configuration statement. This measuring tool changes no validator, model or wire format, and the measurements do not establish new model conformance. The trie library's proofs are assumed sound.

matched-conditions-and-evidence.name: docs-creation-cost/matched-conditions-and-evidence-01
matched-conditions-and-evidence.text: The legs use separate fresh development networks from the same frozen genesis, the same protocol parameters, the same generated wallet funding and the same processing and reclaim windows. Each network is read independently. The receipts include the complete chain-read protocol parameters and the tool versions.

matched-conditions-and-evidence.name: docs-creation-cost/matched-conditions-and-evidence-02
matched-conditions-and-evidence.text: The committed receipts and chain records preserve the transactions, their complete bytes and the network observations. The documentation check recomputes every figure from those bytes, checks the two workloads and regenerates this entire page for comparison. Altered figures and mismatched legs are refused. The hosted registration journey writes the candidate receipt in the same schema and compares its transaction counts and script hashes; fees may differ between runs.

measured-creations.name: docs-creation-cost/measured-creations-01
measured-creations.text: The previous design sent 5 transactions for its first creation and 4 for its later creation. The issue's four-then-two claim does not match these measured counts. The application-held design sent 3 and 1 respectively.

measured-creations.name: docs-creation-cost/measured-creations-02
measured-creations.text: The first creation starts without a live copy of any script it needs. Later creations have the earlier shared copies available. Under the previous design only the state script is shared; request, witness and application scripts are specific to the new registry. The application-held design reuses both the state and application scripts.

measurement-appendix.name: docs-creation-cost/measurement-appendix-01
measurement-appendix.text: The carrying receipt records the test-only producer, its exact source changes and executable hash, the signed transactions, local execution results and independent node answers. The experiment has its own recorded genesis and start time; its protocol parameters match the earlier creation comparison. The receipt checker recomputes lengths, fees, script hashes, placements and execution budgets, binds each transaction to the independent node submission, and requires identical included bytes for every fit. Every refusal must reproduce the node's limiting parameter and figures. Missing forms, missing execution, altered figures and false fits are refused by the hosted documentation check. The test harness is outside the released command's source and changes no production builder or shared receipt.

previous-design.name: docs-creation-cost/previous-design-01
previous-design.text: Release: open-datum 0.16.0 (commit 0c0ab880df982a728b6b89a1e80fc1308144d616). Revision: 0c0ab880df982a728b6b89a1e80fc1308144d616. Deployment blueprint SHA-256: ac43d782181121dcdedfd4a9c48b89fb6fa77dd69e7c9f5619110ca8efb0688b.

transactions-and-reference-outputs.name: docs-creation-cost/transactions-and-reference-outputs-01
transactions-and-reference-outputs.text: Every creation transaction is listed in submission order. Spent and read inputs are output references decoded from that transaction. Each reference output lists the hash computed from its carried script, the script's byte length and its locked lovelace.

what-creating-a-registry-costs.name: docs-creation-cost/what-creating-a-registry-costs-01
what-creating-a-registry-costs.text: As a registry creator, you can compare what the first and a later registry cost under the previous design and the application-held design. The figures below are measured from transactions included on a development network; fees are spent ADA, while ADA locked in reference outputs remains in those outputs.

what-creating-a-registry-costs.name: docs-creation-cost/what-creating-a-registry-costs-02
what-creating-a-registry-costs.text: The two legs run the previous design's last release and this line's release of open datum. Their validators differ: this compares two creation workflows, rather than one release run twice. Within each design, both creations use the same executable and deployment blueprint.

what-the-result-gives-a-creator.name: docs-creation-cost/what-the-result-gives-a-creator-00
what-the-result-gives-a-creator.text: What the result gives a creator.

what-the-result-gives-a-creator.name: docs-creation-cost/what-the-result-gives-a-creator-01
what-the-result-gives-a-creator.text: Each fitting mixed form still needs one prior publication. When a first creation finds no live copy, it cannot skip both publications by carrying: the both-witness form that needs no live reference is refused for size. A fitting mixed form creates no reference output for the script it carries. If a first creation published only the other script, a later registry using the unchanged production command would still have to publish the carried script. Carrying defers that publication; it does not remove it.

what-the-result-gives-a-creator.name: docs-creation-cost/what-the-result-gives-a-creator-02
what-the-result-gives-a-creator.text: The production workflow remains as measured: the first creation sends 3 transactions, and the later creation sends 1 transaction by reusing the shared publications. The measured carrying outcomes are reported without recommending or adopting a mixed form.

witness-publication-overhead.name: docs-creation-cost/witness-publication-overhead-01
witness-publication-overhead.text: The previous design publishes an active witness policy for each registry. That publication is unused by the permanent two-edge contract. Its fee and its reference-output capital are included above and separated below; they must not be added twice. The application-held design publishes no witness policy.

demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.name: docs-demo1/demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-termination-00
demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.text: Demo 1: play a registry from creation to termination.

demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.name: docs-demo1/demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-termination-01
demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.text: As a Cardano developer who knows wallets, faucets and Koios but has never used Singular, you want to watch a registry work before you read how it is built: a registry is created, a key is put in it, changed and ended, the registry refuses what it must refuse, and two people sign their writes in two different ways. Demo 1 introduces that play. The steps, and the programs to run them, live in a repository of their own, singular-demo. This page says what the play shows and where to play it.

the-release-behind-it.name: docs-demo1/the-release-behind-it-01
the-release-behind-it.text: The play runs a release of Singular. These pages are about the release itself, not about the steps: install the commands without Nix and download and verify a release.

what-it-does-not-claim.name: docs-demo1/what-it-does-not-claim-01
what-it-does-not-claim.text: Everything the step-by-step page runs happens on a private test chain that it starts; nothing touches a public network. The open datum application protects the payload and the deposit and nothing more: it demonstrates the registry's mechanics. The receipts of a play are evidence of behaviour on a private chain only, and no complete conformance is claimed here. What the project does claim, and what it leaves open, is on the conformance evidence page. What is deployed on the public preprod network, and the transactions the project's own journeys submitted there, are recorded in the preprod record.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-01
what-the-play-shows.text: Two people, Alice and Bob, share one registry. Its application, open datum, lets a key carry a payload that only the key's controller may replace, and keeps the protected deposit with the live holding. Booking permanent termination donates that deposit to the treasury.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-02
what-the-play-shows.text: A registration starts as a pending request. Any wallet may fold it, making the key active and delivering its token, payload and protected deposit to the committed holding. Its controller may update the payload without spending the registry state.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-03
what-the-play-shows.text: The controller books permanent termination by donating the protected deposit to the treasury and moving the active token into a pending termination request. Any wallet may fold that request, burning its approval and active token and making the key permanently terminal. The folder receives the request's held value and pays the transaction fee. A termination has no reclaim window.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-04
what-the-play-shows.text: A registration that nobody folds can be reclaimed by its refund address inside its reclaim window. After that window, anyone can clean it up: the protected deposit returns to the refund address and the caller receives the held value above that deposit. A reclaim outside its window and a cleanup before its window are refused. The command guide gives the flags and receipts for each operation.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-05
what-the-play-shows.text: The two people sign in the two ways Singular offers. Alice names her vault, a file holding her signing key sealed by a passphrase, and one command builds, signs and sends. Bob names only his wallet's address and a bundle file: the command builds the transactions into the file, signs nothing, and exits with status 19, which means it is waiting for signatures. Then Bob signs the bundle from his vault and sends it, so the machine that builds a write never needs to hold the key.

where-to-play-it.name: docs-demo1/where-to-play-it-01
where-to-play-it.text: The demo repository records its release and the steps it supports. The table lists five entry points: the recorded run to watch, the Killercoda scenario to play in a browser, the step-by-step page to paste from, which needs the programs, and the Nix shell and the Ubuntu kit, which are two ways to get the programs. To play on your own machine, start with the step-by-step page.

where-to-play-it.name: docs-demo1/where-to-play-it-02
where-to-play-it.text: The singular-demo repository describes the shell and the kit, what each is pinned to and what it was tested on.

checked-declaration-register.name: docs-economics-paper/checked-declaration-register-01
checked-declaration-register.text: The entries below are generated from a fresh run of lake env lean tools/axioms.lean over the pinned source, with every cited name confirmed by git show at that revision. Each row uses the full revision above and quotes its axiom line verbatim. Standard axioms are printed as observed; none of these entries contains an additional axiom or sorryAx. Definitions and supplied hand arguments are distinguished from checked declarations in the paper.

checked-declaration-register.name: docs-economics-paper/checked-declaration-register-02
checked-declaration-register.text: The axiom report digest is d22520a04f196bfe52e69ac18d156cce82c78d34f4a6365a16a2138a2815a2f9. The trusted base includes Lean's kernel and the printed axioms, specification adequacy, authentic ledger observations, application authorization and the unproved model-to-validator correspondence. Executable commitment functions are stand-ins; tag counts do not establish cryptographic binding.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-01
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Existing checked declaration: fold routing separates state continuation, exact carrier outputs, donation and ordinary funding. With ordinary inputs I, ordinary outputs O, total tips T and ledger fee f, it proves O + f = I + T and f ≤ I. Donation equals the registration costs plus held-minus-tip for every termination. Ordinary change remains a separate output even at a carrier's address. Ordinary funding and change are lovelace only: the fold and retraction both refuse an unrelated native asset.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-02
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Hand proof supplied: subtracting in the integers gives O − I = T − f. If the processor owns the ordinary funding pool and no other role, that is its monetary net before external costs. It is not a wealth statement about every address receiving an output. The paper's separate net-payoff table includes the booking fee, destination carrier and treasury donation; its rows sum to minus ledger fees, not to request holdings.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-03
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Rejection refunds are added per address, with distinct request inputs and one shared interval. A repeated input or one live compatible member refuses the entire batch. A fold that lands first spends the referenced state output, so an in-flight rejection must be rebuilt; no starvation bound is proved.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-04
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: A zero donation omits the field. Conway transaction-body field 22 accepts a positive donation; optional field 21 is the separate current-treasury assertion. Donation alone does not assert the current treasury balance. The paper cites the exact Conway CDDL revision and its treasury-value check.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-00
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Future work: reusable names and durable evidence.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-01
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Proposed statement: non-terminality. Deleting an active key would let an application reuse its name. This is a proposed extension to a different lifecycle contract, not a way to undo termination in an existing permanent registry.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-02
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Proposed statement: proof durability through witnesses. The other four proposed edges would create an absent witness, change that absent state to active, delete the absent state, and mint a terminal witness on demand. A separate presence witness would be minted with a name's token and burned when the name is terminated or deleted. Absence, presence and termination would then each have an attestation token. These five edges and the presence witness are proposed, not proved functionality of the active contract.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-03
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Hand proof supplied: a transaction referencing the application output holding a name's token loses that input when an application update spends it. A proof against the current registry root similarly depends on a state output that another fold may spend. The goal of the proposed witnesses is to make such evidence more durable. Missing mechanization: their minting, invalidation, custody and verification rules need a future model and implementation evidence. Presence and absence cannot be promised valid after their conditions cease to hold.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-01
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Existing checked declarations: Singular.Statements.retraction_pays_only_the_refund_and_the_fee proves full refund, zero donation, unchanged treasury, fee covered by ordinary funding and balance. If I is that funding, f the fee and P all outputs elsewhere than the refund address, then P ≤ I − f. The model has no wallet-ownership or output-purpose observation: other-address change and third-party payment are indistinguishable, but neither can consume the request's cost or tip. Singular.Statements.pending_registration_can_be_retracted proves existence with explicit reachable-world, pending-request, nonempty-window, signing and funding premises. Neither theorem supplies wallet funds, ledger minima, builder success or inclusion.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-02
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: a request holding 3,000,000 lovelace cannot alone return that amount and pay a 170,000 fee. With 200,000 ordinary funding, the model's construction returns 3,030,000 to the refund address and balances. If the requester owns the refund and funding, its net loss is the booking fee plus the retraction fee, with no processor or treasury allocation. These numbers illustrate the checked construction under its premises, not measured ledger costs.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-03
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: conditional rejection cap. The refund promise is a floor, not an exact split; a processor may leave some tip to the requester. If the transaction additionally balances with zero donation, all outputs outside its refund addresses plus its fee total at most the tips. The paper derives this bound from the summed floors and names balance as an extra premise. Its exact-refund net-payoff illustration is also conditional, not a claim about every accepted rejection.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-04
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: a self-rejecting funder can make the tip an internal transfer, so the design has no universal treasury flood price. Successful junk folds still pay R and occupy turns. Two registrations can race for one key; the loser retains its refund floor, not priority or ownership. A processor's fee can exceed the tip. A rejection sharing a request input with a proposed fold can invalidate that fold despite preserving the state output. Repeated folds can invalidate rejection references indefinitely.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-05
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Proposed statement: the minimum tip should cover measured singleton costs within a declared ledger envelope. The paper derives conditional inequalities for costs and windows, without assuming a minimum service rate or full batches. No measurements establish the selected registration cost, minimum tip or booking-width bound. A later fee or output-minimum change can invalidate the envelope.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-06
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: The application's release rule and custody integration, the open-datum adaptation, the cardano-keri adaptation and validator/builder correspondence with live receipts remain open. The singular tag's fate is decided: mint and delivery on registration, movement at termination booking, burn at termination fold. No key-ownership, squatting, inclusion, priority or application-security guarantee follows from Singular's token counts.

named.name: docs-economics-paper/named-01
named.text: Each token has a name: registering a name mints exactly one token for it, and the registry is the only way to mint it. Holding the token is holding the name. The story is a registered name represented by a token an application holds with its own payload.

named.name: docs-economics-paper/named-02
named.text: Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.insert_active_transaction_row describes the original registry's one minted active asset, its key-derived model name and its destination holding. Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync counts the economic world's actual singular tags across application custody and pending terminations. The register below supplies the exact pin and axiom lines. Missing mechanization: the actual minting policy and name encoding need correspondence evidence; holding the representative proves no legal right or personal identity.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-00
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Named, unique, permanent; permissionless and reusable.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-01
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Singular is a permissionless and reusable mint of named, unique and permanent tokens on Cardano. This is the adopted definition and the paper's organizing promise. The five meanings below distinguish checked model results from application goals and demonstrations.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-02
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Cardano KERI motivates checkpoints selectable by KERI identifier and evidence of whether an identifier was ever convicted on Cardano. For KERI a conviction is a termination, and it is permanent. A lookup of an identifier at a registry root has three outcomes. An active leaf proves that the identifier is registered and not convicted at that root: “not convicted” means active. A terminal leaf proves conviction. An unknown leaf proves only that the identifier is not registered on Singular; that is a different answer and is never presented as “not convicted”. The stored Absent leaf belongs to the extension edges outside the contract of the first release and is not part of this reading. Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.termination keeps a terminal leaf terminal through every later accepted batch, and Singular.Statements.terminal_attestation_permanent keeps a held terminal attestation held and its leaf terminal. Hand proof supplied: by induction over the accepted batches from the genesis state, a key terminal at one reachable state is terminal at every later one, so an active leaf at a root shows the key was never terminal before it: an active identifier was never convicted before that root. Missing mechanization: the lookup is a logical read of the root and verifying a concrete lookup proof is a correspondence obligation; a lookup is valid only against the current root until the next fold; durable attestations are future work, proposed and not proved; Singular alone does not verify duplicity or establish a KERI history, and the consumer integration remains open.

permanent.name: docs-economics-paper/permanent-01
permanent.text: Terminating a name burns its token and records it as terminal; it can never be issued again. Alice terminates her name, then tries to register it again and is refused. For KERI, termination is intended to be conviction: the convicted identifier must never come back in that registry.

permanent.name: docs-economics-paper/permanent-02
permanent.text: Hand proof supplied: read as a lookup, a terminal leaf proves conviction and an active leaf at a reachable root shows the key was never terminal before it; an unknown leaf proves only that the identifier is not registered. Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.termination refuses requests at a terminal key in a reachable original registry and preserves its terminal leaf through later accepted batches. Singular.Statements.booked_termination_foldable supplies a conditional economic fold making the key terminal, and Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync then gives zero supply. Missing mechanization: KERI's conviction and custody release require application evidence. The economic termination donates everything held except the tip, as Singular.Statements.fold_routes_every_amount states; Alice receives no deposit back.

permissionless.name: docs-economics-paper/permissionless-01
permissionless.text: Anyone creates a registry, anyone books a name, anyone settles pending requests, all from public chain data. The creator has no power over the names. These participation promises remain subject to application authorization, funding and admission. Bob, who did not create the registry, settles pending requests, Alice's included.

permissionless.name: docs-economics-paper/permissionless-02
permissionless.text: Existing checked declarations: Singular.Statements.fold_inputs_public equates the original builder with construction from its public view; Singular.Statements.fold_requires_no_signer proves empty required signers and invariance under changed approval signatures. Missing mechanization: these are original-builder results, not an economic-builder public-data theorem or a running demonstration. Creation, chain-data retrieval and Bob's actual batch require off-chain and validator evidence. No inclusion guarantee follows.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-01
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: Let R be the registration cost, t the declared tip, and a the declared carrier lovelace. Booking enforces the fixed minimum tip. The carrier amount follows actual ledger minimum rules; the model proves exact declared amounts and does not compute those minima.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-02
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: A registration's application tag commits to its payload and nonce; its trie-ready tag commits to the operation and the same nonce. Both are minted in the same booking and burned on every exit. Application tags minted elsewhere are outside Singular's supply guarantee and cannot substitute for this booking. Termination booking moves the singular tag from custody; its fold burns that tag and the trie-ready tag. A registration fold mints the singular tag at the booked destination with the declared carrier and datum.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-03
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: The fixed parameters are registration cost, minimum tip, maximum booking width, processing and reclaim windows, policy bindings and registry identity. The minimum tip retains the wire key maxFee. There is no parameter-update or migration authority. The paper treats the maximum booking width being smaller than the processing window as a sizing criterion, distinct from the checked booking-width bound.

reusable.name: docs-economics-paper/reusable-01
reusable.text: The same mint serves any application: open-datum today, a closed variant in the demonstration, KERI checkpoints next, with no change to its contract. Each name's token lives in its owner's application, which decides what the name points to.

reusable.name: docs-economics-paper/reusable-02
reusable.text: Missing mechanization: the concrete application demonstration uses a closed flag on the same release and commands. It sets the payload at registration, refuses every update and leaves only termination. This is application-validator and executable behavior outside the checked registry model; this paper asserts no release or running-demonstration receipt. KERI integration and serving both application kinds in one registry through application tags remain future work.

singular-registry-design-and-economics.name: docs-economics-paper/singular-registry-design-and-economics-01
singular-registry-design-and-economics.text: As a reviewer, read this page to learn what a registration or termination commits, where its tokens and lovelace go, and which promises have checked evidence. The paper explains the complete mechanism, its assumptions and its counterexamples: download the paper PDF. The documentation build compiles the PDF from the committed LaTeX sources using the llncs class.

singular-registry-design-and-economics.name: docs-economics-paper/singular-registry-design-and-economics-02
singular-registry-design-and-economics.text: Implementation standing: not yet conformant. The validators and builders still implement superseded economic rules. The conformance evidence keeps affected requirements unmet; a Lean proof is not a ledger receipt or deployment acceptance.

the-mechanism-at-a-glance.name: docs-economics-paper/the-mechanism-at-a-glance-01
the-mechanism-at-a-glance.text: The registry records a permanent lifecycle. Registration changes an unknown key to active; termination changes an active key to terminal. The application authorizes registration and controls the resulting singular tag. It consents to termination by releasing that genuine tag into a request. Singular does not judge the application's release rule. Checked lifecycle and custody evidence appears in the declaration register below.

the-mechanism-at-a-glance.name: docs-economics-paper/the-mechanism-at-a-glance-02
the-mechanism-at-a-glance.text: Pending requests occupy their own outputs. Folds spend and continue the registry state output. Rejection reads that output by reference and spends only the rejected registrations. It needs a current lifecycle mismatch or expiry after both registration windows. Compatible registrations are protected through the reclaim window; a lost race can create a mismatch earlier. A termination has no rejection, retraction or expiry exit.

unique.name: docs-economics-paper/unique-01
unique.text: A name can be taken only with a proof that it is absent, so two people cannot hold separate genuine tokens for the same name in one registry. Bob tries to register Alice's already registered name and is refused.

unique.name: docs-economics-paper/unique-02
unique.text: Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.insert_active_transaction_row refuses a subsequent approved registration of the same key with key-exists. Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync bounds economic supply by one, including a token in a pending termination. Missing mechanization: actual absence-proof verification is a validator correspondence obligation. “Absent” in this story means unknown and untaken, not the historical stored Absent leaf. Booking does not reserve a name or establish who ought to own it.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-00
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: What is checked, and at what strength.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-01
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: Existing checked declaration means the register below quotes the declaration's fresh axiom result at the exact model pin. Hand proof supplied means the paper gives an argument and its premises. Proposed statement means a conditional design or sizing criterion. Missing mechanization marks an unproved boundary. These four labels do not imply implementation conformance.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-02
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: The exact model revision is 4254a3073fe0457946eba0a68d974c999c930ebf, the last ancestor commit changing the model, checked with Lean 4.27.0. Economic reachability starts from any reachable original registry with empty pending pools and a zero treasury counter, then admits bookings, rejections, retractions and economic folds. It does not claim a complete economic history from ledger genesis.

appendix-regenerate-this-page.name: docs-folding-requests/appendix-regenerate-this-page-01
appendix-regenerate-this-page.text: The measurement job re-evaluates the kept transactions and captures a fresh boundary for each kind. The documentation check regenerates the marked block and refuses differences in either the page or the receipt. To refresh the block explicitly, run python3 tools/batch_limits.py --write, then regenerate the page's speech and changed narration.

choose-a-named-batch.name: docs-folding-requests/choose-a-named-batch-01
choose-a-named-batch.text: Repeat --pending to choose the entire ordered batch yourself. It is built as named or refused, never trimmed, even if you also give --limit.

discover-and-fold.name: docs-folding-requests/discover-and-fold-01
discover-and-fold.text: Give the registry's address, the release blueprint, your provider and your own wallet. Your wallet need not have booked any request. Registrations and terminations of this registry can share a transaction when their keys differ.

discover-and-fold.name: docs-folding-requests/discover-and-fold-02
discover-and-fold.text: Requests are ordered by your take, greatest first, with output references breaking ties. A registration's take is the request's held ADA above the deposit its holding must keep. A termination's take is the request's whole held ADA. Your wallet receives the transaction's change and pays its fee; the gross take is not the same as profit after that fee.

discover-and-fold.name: docs-folding-requests/discover-and-fold-03
discover-and-fold.text: To cap discovery, give the maximum number you want in --limit. The cap does not promise that many will fit.

discover-and-fold.name: docs-folding-requests/discover-and-fold-04
discover-and-fold.text: Only exceeding a transaction size, memory or steps limit permits a shorter prefix. A failed public read, failed registry replay or another construction error stops with its own reason. It never becomes an empty or shorter answer. The current network decides what fits; the measured workload below is not a fixed cap built into this command.

fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.name: docs-folding-requests/fold-pending-requests-from-public-data-00
fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.text: Fold pending requests from public data.

fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.name: docs-folding-requests/fold-pending-requests-from-public-data-01
fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.text: As a folder, you find a registry's pending requests from public data without a file from anyone who booked them. You fold as many as fit, keep each request's value above what the application requires, and can read the measured limit before deciding what to fold.

fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.name: docs-folding-requests/fold-pending-requests-from-public-data-02
fold-pending-requests-from-public-data.text: The flow starts with public holders of the application's approvals. Discovery names the holders and requests it skips, orders the foldable requests by your take, and tries prefixes until it finds the largest fitting batch. The receipt accounts for what folded, what was skipped and what is left.

read-the-fold-receipt.name: docs-folding-requests/read-the-fold-receipt-01
read-the-fold-receipt.text: The receipt names the registry's new root and state output. Its folded list names the key, request kind and pending output reference of every folded request. Its skipped list names each omitted holder's reference and reason. Its left count is the foldable requests beyond the chosen prefix. A skipped request is never counted as left.

read-the-fold-receipt.name: docs-folding-requests/read-the-fold-receipt-02
read-the-fold-receipt.text: Automatic discovery skips these kinds of holder or request and keeps folding the rest. A named batch instead refuses a bad request.

read-the-fold-receipt.name: docs-folding-requests/read-the-fold-receipt-03
